title: Terraform Associate vs AZ-400: Which DevOps Cert?
subtitle: Pure IaC (HashiCorp) or the full Microsoft ecosystem — which will serve you better?

pros: The reference IaC cert — Terraform is the de facto standard in 2026 (multi-cloud, multi-provider).
A cheap exam ($70) you can prepare in 30-50 hours if you've used Terraform in production.
Cloud-agnostic: it opens AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, and every modern SaaS (Datadog, Cloudflare, etc.).
Senior DevOps median salary of €65k in France, €85k in Luxembourg (Hays 2026).
cons: Does NOT qualify you on the other DevOps components: CI/CD, monitoring, pipeline security, secrets management.
The cert alone (without production Terraform experience) is valued little — it counts for less than 'you've shipped to production'.
The 003 exam emphasizes Terraform Cloud / Sentinel — if you've only used open-source Terraform, expect ~15-20% surprises.
certs.bestFor: You're targeting multi-cloud DevOps / Platform Engineer / SRE roles. You want the IaC cert that follows you everywhere.

pros: Covers the whole Azure DevOps ecosystem: Azure DevOps (Pipelines, Boards, Repos), GitHub Actions, monitoring, security, governance.
Expert level (advanced cert) — a bigger salary premium (~€10-15k vs Associate level).
Recognized at Microsoft-committed organizations (banking, public sector, large industrials).
Pairs well with the AZ-104 + AZ-204 for a 'full-stack Azure' profile.
cons: Prerequisite: you must already hold the AZ-104 or AZ-204 — otherwise, much longer study.
Very Azure-centric: transfers poorly outside the Microsoft ecosystem.
The exam changes regularly with GitHub / Azure DevOps updates.
certs.bestFor: You're already on Azure (AZ-104/AZ-204 in hand) and targeting a senior DevOps role in a Microsoft environment.

verdicts.profile: You work in a multi-cloud or cloud-native environment.
verdicts.why: Terraform works with AWS, Azure, GCP, K8s, and 500+ providers. The AZ-400 only helps in a Microsoft environment.

verdicts.profile: You're already at a Microsoft shop (Azure DevOps + Azure cloud).
verdicts.why: Make the most of your current stack. The cert covers exactly the tools you already use (Pipelines, Repos, Boards, Test Plans).

verdicts.profile: You're new to DevOps and want the most 'learnable' cert.
verdicts.why: $70, 50 hours of realistic prep, a multiple-choice exam (no hands-on lab). Far more accessible than the AZ-400 (an Expert cert that assumes the AZ-104).

verdicts.profile: You're targeting multi-client DevOps freelance / consulting.
verdicts.why: Freelance DevOps engagements are rarely Azure-only. Terraform is more versatile and more in demand at 2026 day rates (Free-Work data).

verdicts.profile: You're targeting a Senior / Lead DevOps role at a large Microsoft-centric enterprise (banking, insurance).
verdicts.why: At that level, the complete Microsoft ecosystem is expected. The AZ-400 proves your command of the internal tooling beyond IaC.

verdicts.profile: You want both — where to start?
verdicts.why: Terraform first (fast, cheap, and it lays the IaC foundations you'll use for the AZ-400 afterward). The AZ-400 takes an extra 3-6 months.

tldr: Terraform = a pure IaC cert: multi-cloud, cheap, accessible. AZ-400 = the complete Microsoft DevOps cert, Expert level, focused on the Azure ecosystem. If you're starting out or want versatility, Terraform. If you live in Azure and are targeting senior+, AZ-400.
